newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO, U.S. inaugurate Gaza industrial zone.
newsitem.headline: PLO, U.S. inaugurate Gaza industrial zone.

text.p: Palestinian and U.S. officials on Friday broke ground for an industrial zone in the Gaza Strip self-rule enclave intended to create 17,000 jobs.

Palestinian President Yasser Arafat, U.S. Ambassador Martin Indyk and U.S. Consul-General Edward Abington attended the inauguration ceremony for the Gaza Industrial Estate near the Karni commercial checkpoint between Israel and Gaza.
"With God's help within the coming six months we will establish the industrial premises of this area. This project will employ 17,000 workers permanently," Arafat said.
The Palestinian Authority donated the land for the 50 hectare (124 acre) industrial park, to be funded by the private sector and international donors.

The Palestine Development and Investment Company (PADICO) said it would invest $30 million to develop the industrial park. The U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID) has pledged $6 million for Palestinian industrial estates.
